steps.title: Main Dashboard Graph
steps.body: This is the main Trellis Dashboard Graph — you'll see this same graph on many of the reports in Trellis. Hover over any date to see the variety of metrics available.

steps.title: Date Selector
steps.body: You can adjust the date range of this graph by using the Date Selector. Pick any date range you'd like, and compare to any other dates you'd like. Try clicking it now!

steps.title: Customize Your Metrics
steps.body: If you would like to change any of the metrics on the Dashboard, that can be found by clicking these three buttons. From there you can add any metrics you'd like!

steps.title: Welcome to Your Ad
steps.body: This is your Individual Ad page — your command center for a single campaign. Here you can view performance, manage targets, and configure every aspect of how this ad runs. Let's take a quick tour of what's available.

steps.title: Products
steps.body: The Products tab shows you all of the products included in this ad campaign. You can see each product's performance metrics, review which ASINs are actively being advertised, and manage your product selection.

steps.title: Keyword Targets
steps.body: The Keyword Targets tab shows all of the keywords and negative keywords in this campaign, along with their individual bids and performance metrics. This is where Trellis manages and optimizes your keyword targeting.

steps.title: Product Targets
steps.body: The Product Targets tab shows your ASIN and category targets, along with any negative targets. Use this to see where Trellis is targeting your ads at the product level and how each target is performing.

steps.title: Placement Report
steps.body: The Placement Report shows you exactly where your ad is appearing — top of search, product pages, rest of search — and the individual metrics for each placement. Great for understanding where your spend is going.

steps.title: Search Term Report
steps.body: The Search Term Report shows the actual customer search queries that triggered this campaign, along with their metrics and trends. This is one of the most powerful views for understanding what is and isn't working.

steps.title: Configuration
steps.body: The Configuration tab is where all of your campaign settings live — budget, ACOS targets, optimization strategy, bid ranges, and much more. This tab has its own dedicated tour. Head there and launch the Page Tour from the Trellis Help panel to get a full walkthrough!

steps.title: Welcome to Configuration
steps.body: You're now in the Configuration tab — your control center for every aspect of how this campaign operates. The left sidebar is your navigation menu. Let's walk through each section.

steps.title: Media Plan
steps.body: The Media Plan section is the main settings panel for your campaign. Here you define your campaign title, optimization strategy, ACOS range targets, daily budget, which products are included, and your targeting setup. This is where most of your day-to-day configuration lives.

steps.title: Advanced Options
steps.body: Within the Media Plan section, the Advanced Options accordion reveals powerful controls: Discovery & Harvesting, Optimization Strategy, Match Types, Bid Ranges, Amazon bidding options, and more. These give you fine-grained control over how Trellis manages your campaign.

steps.title: Notifications
steps.body: The Notifications section lets you set up performance alerts for this campaign. Configure triggers for events like ACOS exceeding a threshold or spend going over a limit — so you and your team are proactively notified when something needs attention.

steps.title: Rules
steps.body: Rules let you create custom automation logic for your campaign. Set conditions and actions that override or supplement Trellis's default bidding behavior — for example, pausing keywords that exceed a certain CPA, or applying a bid modifier when a product goes out of stock.

steps.title: Harvesting Programs
steps.body: Harvesting Programs control how Trellis discovers and adds new keywords and ASINs to your campaign. Set the thresholds for when a search term gets harvested, and customize the logic for how newly discovered targets are managed after they're added.

steps.title: Weekday Parting
steps.body: Weekday Parting lets you set bid multipliers based on the day of the week. If your products consistently perform better on certain days, you can increase or decrease bids accordingly to maximize your return on ad spend.

steps.title: Dayparting
steps.body: Dayparting gives you hourly bid multipliers across a 24-hour schedule. Use your campaign's hourly performance data to increase bids during peak-converting hours and reduce them during off-peak times — maximizing efficiency throughout the day.

steps.title: Serving Hours
steps.body: Serving Hours lets you restrict when your ads are eligible to run. If you only want ads active during specific windows — for example, during business hours when your team can fulfill orders — you can set those restrictions here.

steps.title: Scheduled Updates
steps.body: Scheduled Updates let you plan future configuration changes in advance. Schedule budget increases for a product launch, ACOS adjustments ahead of a promo period, or strategy switches — all without needing to be online when the change takes effect.

steps.title: History
steps.body: The History section is a complete log of every change made to this campaign — by you, your team, or Trellis automatically. Use it to audit changes, understand why performance shifted on a given date, and track who made what modifications.

steps.title: Welcome to the Advertisement Report
steps.body: This is your master view of all Media Plans. From here you can monitor performance across every campaign, use smart filters to surface what needs attention, and take action on many campaigns at once with Bulk Actions. Let's walk through the key features.

steps.title: Date Range & Period Comparison
steps.body: Set the reporting period here. All metrics, charts, and table data update instantly to reflect your chosen range. The comparison option shows performance vs. a prior period — the green and red indicators on each metric tell you whether things are improving or declining.

steps.title: Key Performance Summary
steps.body: The six metric cards at the top show your totals for the selected period: Ad Sales, Ad Spend, ROAS, ACOS, Clicks, and Impressions. Each card includes a comparison to the prior period so you can quickly gauge whether performance is trending in the right direction.

steps.title: Performance Overview Chart
steps.body: This chart plots your key metrics day-by-day over the selected period. Hover any data point to see exact numbers for that date. Use the legend below the chart to toggle which metrics are visible — helpful for isolating trends like ACOS or Ad Spend over time.

steps.title: Smart Filter Tabs
steps.body: These tabs instantly segment all your Media Plans by status. 'New' shows recently created campaigns. 'Trending Up' and 'Trending Down' flag recent momentum shifts. 'High ACOS', 'Low ACOS', and 'ACOS in Range' help you prioritize optimization work. 'Low Budget' catches campaigns that may soon pause. Each badge shows the live count.

steps.title: Table Controls
steps.body: Use the search bar to find specific campaigns by name. The gear icon lets you customize which columns are visible. Click '+ Add Filter' to create custom conditions — filter by ACOS range, spend level, state, or any other metric to build exactly the view you need.

steps.title: Selecting Campaigns for Bulk Actions
steps.body: The header checkbox selects all visible campaigns at once — individual row checkboxes let you pick specific ones. Once at least one row is selected, the Bulk Actions button in the top-right becomes active. We'll use it in the next step.

steps.title: Bulk Actions — Manage at Scale
steps.body: With campaigns selected, Bulk Actions lets you apply changes to all of them simultaneously. You can update: State (pause or enable), Performance Targets (ACOS range), Budget (including scheduling future updates), Categorization (tags and categories), Bidding (programs, algorithm, modifiers, strategy), Dayparting & Placement multipliers, and Automation settings — all in one operation across every selected campaign.

steps.title: Welcome to the Product Report
steps.body: This is your full-catalog performance view. Unlike the Ad Report which covers only advertised campaigns, the Product Report shows every product — combining organic and paid data side by side. Use it to understand true profitability, spot under-advertised products, and organize your catalog. Let's walk through the key features.

steps.title: Date Range & Period Comparison
steps.body: Set the reporting window here. All metrics, the chart, and table data update instantly. The comparison mode shows performance vs. a prior period — the green and red indicators on each metric card tell you at a glance whether things are trending up or down.

steps.title: Key Performance Metrics
steps.body: The six metric cards summarize your catalog's performance for the selected period: Ad Sales, Ad Spend, Cost (your total COGS), ROAS, ACOS, and Clicks. Pay attention to Total ACOS — it measures ad spend against all sales including organic, giving you a truer picture of advertising efficiency than Ad ACOS alone.

steps.title: Performance Overview Chart
steps.body: This chart plots your key metrics day-by-day across the selected period. Hover any data point to see exact figures for that date. Toggle metrics on and off using the legend below the chart to focus on trends that matter most — like isolating ACOS trajectory or comparing Ad Sales to Ad Spend over time.

steps.title: Group By — Segment Your View
steps.body: This is unique to the Product Report. The Group By dropdown lets you switch between three views: By Product (all variants rolled up under one listing), By ASIN (each individual variant as its own row), and By Parent ASIN (grouped by parent). Use this to drill from a high-level product view down to the specific variations driving — or dragging — your performance.

steps.title: Table Controls & Filtering
steps.body: Use the search bar to find products by name or ASIN. The gear icon lets you customize which columns are visible. Click '+ Add Filter' to narrow the table by any metric or attribute — filter by tag, enrollment status, ACOS range, sales threshold, and more. Combine multiple filters to build exactly the view you need.

steps.title: Selecting Products for Bulk Actions
steps.body: The header checkbox selects all visible products at once — individual row checkboxes let you pick specific ones. Once at least one product is selected, the Bulk Actions button in the top-right activates. We'll use it in the next step.

steps.title: Bulk Actions — Tag, Organize & Enroll
steps.body: With products selected, Bulk Actions lets you make changes across your entire selection at once. You can: Add or Remove Tags (to group products into sets you can filter and report on), Enroll products in NTM (New to Marketplace) campaigns to expand reach, and manage product Categorization. Tags are one of the most powerful organizational tools in Trellis — use them to label seasonal items, high-margin SKUs, new launches, and more.

steps.title: Welcome to the Goals Dashboard
steps.body: This is where you set monthly performance targets — for Total Sales, Ad Spend, and TACOS — and track real-time pacing throughout the month. If you haven't configured goals yet, the Configuration tab is the place to start. Once goals are set, this page becomes your go-to for checking whether you're on track to hit your numbers.

steps.title: Three Views
steps.body: The page has three tabs: Details shows pacing charts and category breakdowns for the selected month. Overview shows the full year at a glance in a single table, so you can compare month-to-month targets and actuals. Configuration is where you enter your monthly targets.

steps.title: Month Navigator
steps.body: Use the arrows to move between months. Clicking back lets you review pacing from prior months — helpful for spotting seasonal trends, auditing performance against historical goals, or comparing how this month is tracking vs the same month last year.

steps.title: Sales Goal Pacing
steps.body: The gauge shows your current pacing percentage — how your actual month-to-date sales compare to what you should have by this point in the month, given your goal. The line chart plots actual daily sales (solid line) against the expected trajectory (dashed). If the solid line is tracking below the dashed line, you may need to increase ad investment to close the gap before month-end.

steps.title: Ad Spend Budget & TACOS
steps.body: Below the Sales chart are two more trackers. Ad Spend Budget shows whether you're over or under-pacing on spend for the month — useful for catching runaway spend or spotting under-investment. TACOS shows your total ad cost as a percentage of total sales vs your target efficiency. A color-coded bar in each section gives you an instant visual on where you stand.

steps.title: Category Goals
steps.body: At the bottom of the Details tab is a per-category breakdown. For each category, you can see actual Sales, Ad Spend, and TACOS alongside any category-level targets you've set. Click the pencil icon on any row to set or edit that category's goals. Click the expand arrow on a row to drill into the individual products within that category.

steps.title: Configuration — Set Your Targets
steps.body: The Configuration tab is where you enter your monthly targets. For each month, fill in your Total Sales goal ($), TACoS target (%), and Ad Spend budget ($). The copy icon at the end of each row fills the same value into all subsequent months — handy for quickly setting a consistent annual target. Hit Submit when you're done to save.
